nodes.label: Modular Arithmetic
nodes.rationale: Turns unbounded numbers into fixed-size ones while preserving ring structure. Division is not well-defined — it needs an inverse, which exists iff gcd(b,m)=1, which is why prime moduli like 10^9+7 and 998244353 are ubiquitous.

nodes.label: Modular Exponentiation (modpow / exponentiation by squaring)
nodes.source_location: The six routines worth writing once
nodes.rationale: Theta(log e) and works for any associative operation — integers, matrices, function composition. Must compute in u128 because two values below 10^9+7 multiply to nearly 10^18.

nodes.label: Modular Inverse via Fermat's Little Theorem
nodes.source_location: The six routines worth writing once
nodes.rationale: inv(a) = a^(m-2) mod m requires m PRIME. With a composite modulus it is silently wrong for any b not coprime to m — and right for coprime b, so tests often pass. Measured: 100,000 inverses took 23.1 ms.

nodes.label: Extended Euclidean Algorithm
nodes.source_location: The six routines worth writing once
nodes.rationale: Computes an inverse for any b coprime to m and reports failure when gcd(b,m) != 1, rather than returning garbage the way a Fermat modpow would with a composite modulus.

nodes.label: Sieve of Eratosthenes
nodes.source_location: The six routines worth writing once
nodes.rationale: Batch algorithm: Theta(n log log n) for all primes <= n. Two details halve the work — start marking at i^2, stop the outer loop at sqrt(n). Measured 20.49 ms for primes below 10^7 (664,579 primes), ~172x faster than trial division.

nodes.label: Miller-Rabin Primality Test
nodes.rationale: Single-number test at Theta(k log^3 n) with error 4^-k; size-bound rather than range-bound, which is the opposite of a sieve. Choosing wrongly is 100x in one direction and impossible in the other.

nodes.label: nCr with Precomputed Factorials
nodes.source_location: The six routines worth writing once
nodes.rationale: The inverse-factorial trick: compute inv_fact[n] with ONE modpow, then walk backwards with inv_fact[i-1] = inv_fact[i] * i. Theta(n + log m) instead of Theta(n log m).

nodes.label: Matrix Exponentiation for Linear Recurrences
nodes.rationale: A k-term linear recurrence becomes a k x k matrix power, giving Theta(k^3 log n) — n = 10^18 is ~60 matrix multiplications. The dynamic-programming 'amortize it' lens taken to its conclusion.

nodes.label: FFT / NTT Convolution
nodes.rationale: Widest reach of the toolkit: Theta(n log n) convolution underlies bignum multiplication, polynomial arithmetic, signal processing, wildcard string matching. NTT is the same algorithm over a modular ring, avoiding floating-point error entirely — the right choice for integer inputs.

nodes.label: Overflow Before the Modulus (u128 reduction)
nodes.rationale: The modulus is applied after the multiplication, so the intermediate must fit. u64 holds one product of two sub-10^9 values but not three. Fix: compute in u128, or wrap the modulus in a newtype so every operation reduces by construction. Montgomery/Barrett reduction is the after-measurement optimization.

nodes.label: Rust % is a Remainder, Not a Modulus
nodes.rationale: % takes the sign of the dividend, so (a - b) % m is negative when a < b — a negative index panic or wrong branch. Always (a + m - b) % m, or rem_euclid.
